item.title: Iran caps Hormuz transit at 15 ships a day under ceasefire
item.description:
Iran will permit no more than 15 vessels per day to transit the Strait of Hormuz under the two-week ceasefire it agreed with the United States, a senior Iranian source told Russia's TASS news agency on Thursday. The cap, enforced under the supervision of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, represents barely a tenth of the roughly 130 ships that crossed the waterway daily before the conflict began on 28 February.

"Under the current ceasefire, fewer than 15 ships per day are permitted to transit the Strait of Hormuz. This movement is strictly contingent upon Iran's approval and the enforcement of a specific protocol," the unnamed Iranian source said, adding: "There will be no return to the pre-war status quo."

item.title: Study finds low oxygen can trigger limb regeneration in mice
item.description: Salamanders and frog tadpoles can regrow entire limbs after amputation. Mammals cannot. A new study published April 8 in Science offers an explanation rooted not in genetics, but in how cells sense oxygen — and demonstrates that tweaking that response can awaken dormant regenerative programs in mouse tissue.

item.title: Xi Jinping meets Taiwan's KMT leader in Beijing
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping met Kuomintang Chairwoman Cheng Li-wun at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing on Friday, marking the first meeting between a sitting KMT leader and China's Communist Party chief in nearly a decade. The encounter caps a week-long diplomatic push by Cheng, who has framed her six-day trip as a "journey for peace" aimed at easing military tensions across the Taiwan Strait.

item.title: Bank of Korea holds rates as BOJ flags stagflation risk
item.description: The Bank of Korea held its benchmark interest rate steady on Friday while the Bank of Japan's deputy governor warned of stagflation risks, as the ongoing Middle East conflict continues to ripple through Asian economies via surging energy prices.

item.title: TSMC Q1 revenue jumps 35%, beating forecasts on AI demand
item.description:
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. reported first-quarter revenue of NT$1.134 trillion ($35.71 billion) on Thursday, a 35 percent jump from the same period a year earlier that topped analyst expectations, according to Reuters. Bloomberg reported that analysts had estimated NT$1.12 trillion on average.

The results suggest that global demand for artificial intelligence chips remained resilient even as geopolitical uncertainty stemming from conflict in the Middle East weighed on broader markets earlier in the quarter.

item.title: Trump accuses Iran of violating Strait of Hormuz deal
item.description: President Donald Trump accused Iran on Thursday of failing to honor its ceasefire commitment to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, escalating a war of words that has sent oil prices climbing back toward $100 a barrel and dampened the market optimism that greeted the truce just two days earlier.

item.title: Gold heads for third weekly gain as U.S.-Iran truce wobbles
item.description: Gold was on track for a third consecutive weekly gain on Thursday as traders weighed the prospects of a lasting ceasefire between the United States and Iran, while a weakening dollar lifted Asian currencies across the board.

item.title: Artemis II crew set to splash down today after Moon flyby
item.description: Teledyne Technologies announced on Wednesday that its subsidiaries are providing an array of mission-critical hardware for NASA's Artemis II, the first crewed voyage around the Moon since Apollo 17 in December 1972. The announcement came as the four-person crew hurtled back toward Earth, with splashdown in the Pacific Ocean scheduled for Friday afternoon.

item.title: Finland begins trial run at world's first permanent nuclear waste site
item.description: After more than two decades of construction, Finland is on the verge of opening Onkalo, the world's first facility designed for the permanent underground disposal of spent nuclear fuel. Authorities are expected to grant an operating license within months, according to the Associated Press, marking a milestone in the long-running global challenge of what to do with radioactive waste.

item.title: First-ever egg from a mammal ancestor found in 250M-year-old fossil
item.description: A 250-million-year-old fossilized egg containing an embryo of Lystrosaurus, a stocky, tusked creature that dominated Earth after its worst mass extinction, has provided the first direct evidence that mammal ancestors laid eggs. The findings, published Wednesday in the journal PLOS ONE, resolve a question that has eluded evolutionary biologists for nearly two centuries.

item.title: TotalEnergies shuts SATORP refinery after Iran strike damages processing train
item.description: TotalEnergies announced on Thursday that the SATORP refinery in Jubail, Saudi Arabia, was shut down after sustaining damage during the night of April 7 to 8, marking the latest blow to the kingdom's energy infrastructure from the ongoing Iran conflict.

item.title: Dubai caps foreign airlines at one daily flight until May 31
item.description: Dubai has restricted foreign airlines to a single daily flight to its airports until May 31, according to confidential correspondence reviewed by Reuters, a move that extends wartime constraints on the world's busiest international aviation hub and deals the heaviest blow to Indian carriers.

item.title: Strait of Hormuz remains closed despite ceasefire as Iran imposes ship tolls
item.description: Days after the United States and Iran agreed to a two-week ceasefire, the Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed, with Iran imposing transit fees of up to $2 million per vessel and limiting passage to a handful of ships under tight military supervision. The toll system, which maritime law experts and the United Nations' shipping agency have called a violation of international law, has dashed hopes that the truce would restore normal traffic through the waterway that carries roughly a fifth of the world's oil and gas supply.

item.title: Oil spill shuts down Port of Antwerp, Europe's No. 2 cargo hub
item.description: An oil spill during a bunkering operation at the Port of Antwerp-Bruges has shut down a stretch of the River Scheldt and closed critical locks, leaving Europe's second-largest cargo port inaccessible by water and disrupting dozens of vessels on Friday.

item.title: IDF chief says Israel is 'in a state of war' in Lebanon, not a ceasefire
item.description: Rockets fired from Lebanon struck northern Israel on Friday, causing power outages across the towns of Kiryat Shmona and Metula, according to Israeli Channel 12. The barrage damaged a building in Metula and sparked a fire at the scene, though no casualties were reported. The strike was part of an intensifying pattern of Hezbollah rocket fire that has made daily life in Israel's northern border communities increasingly untenable.

item.title: Zelenskyy confirms Ukraine shot down Iranian drones in Middle East
item.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy publicly confirmed for the first time that Ukrainian military personnel actively shot down Iranian-designed Shahed drones in multiple Middle Eastern countries, marking a dramatic expansion of Kyiv's role in the broader conflict with Tehran. Zelenskyy made the remarks to reporters on Wednesday in a briefing embargoed until Friday, according to the Associated Press.

"Did we destroy Iranian Shaheds? Yes, we did. Did we do it in just one country? No, in several," Zelenskyy said, as reported by Euronews. He described the operations not as training exercises but as "support in building a modern air defence system that can actually work."

item.title: EU and US near critical minerals deal to counter China
item.description: The European Union and the United States are closing in on an agreement to coordinate on producing and securing critical minerals, according to a draft action plan seen by Bloomberg on Thursday. The deal is part of a broader trilateral push with Japan to break dependence on Chinese supplies of materials essential to defense, clean energy and advanced technology.

item.title: Ocean temperatures hit near-record highs in March, signaling El Niño shift
item.description: Global sea surface temperatures reached their second-highest levels on record for March, the European Union's Copernicus Climate Change Service reported on Friday, pointing to a likely transition toward El Niño conditions that could push global temperatures to new highs later this year.

item.title: Vance departs for Iran peace talks as Lebanon crisis threatens ceasefire
item.description: Vice President JD Vance departed Friday aboard Air Force Two for Islamabad, Pakistan, where he will lead what officials describe as one of the most direct US-Iran engagements since the 1979 Islamic Revolution. The first round of talks is scheduled for Saturday morning local time, with a fragile two-week ceasefire already showing signs of fracture.

item.title: Hezbollah vows to fight 'until last breath' ahead of Israel-Lebanon talks
item.description: Hezbollah Secretary-General Naim Qassem on Friday called on Lebanese officials to stop offering "free concessions" to Israel and vowed that "the resistance will continue until our last breath," sharpening the group's rhetoric just days before Israel and Lebanon are set to hold direct negotiations in Washington.
